title: Format a value with a pattern switch

blocks.text: Java 21's pattern matching for `switch` (JEP 441) switches on any object with type patterns (`case Integer i`), guards (`case Integer i when i < 0`) and `case null`. The page's pitfalls: without a `case null`, a `null` selector throws `NullPointerException`, because **`default` does not match `null`**; and the first matching case wins, so the compiler rejects a plain `case Integer i` placed before a guarded `case Integer i when ...`.

rows: a blank `String` (empty, or only whitespace, Unicode spaces included)

blocks.text: For example, `format(-5)` is `"negative integer -5"`, `format(0)` is `"non-negative integer 0"`, `format("  ")` is `"blank string"` and `format(2.5)` is `"other: Double"`. Only a `List` has list rows: a `Set` is "anything else".

cases.says: Integers, strings, lists and other values each get the description of the first case that matches them.
null is formatted as "null" instead of throwing NullPointerException.
A string of only whitespace, Unicode spaces such as EM SPACE (U+2003) included, is a blank string.

origin.section: Q2: Explain pattern matching for switch with examples of guarded patterns and null handling.

concepts: A pattern switch throws NullPointerException on null unless it has case null, because default does not match null.
A switch matches any object by type patterns with when guards, and the first matching case wins.
